changes.before: Complete conditionalReply(currentTag, suppliedTag). For an exact matching supplied ETag return {status:304, body:null, etag:currentTag}; otherwise return {status:200, body:{title:"Public note"}, etag:currentTag}. This simplified contract accepts one exact strong tag or a missing tag, not comma lists, weak tags, or wildcard matching.
changes.after: An ETag labels a version of a response. A matching tag lets the browser reuse its saved copy.

before: An ETag is a response validator identifying a version of a representation. It is not necessarily a timestamp.
A client can send its saved tag in If-None-Match to ask whether that representation changed.
For a matching GET validator, a server can respond 304 Not Modified without sending the representation body again. The client can reuse its stored representation.
When the tag differs, a normal 200 response sends the representation and its current tag. A changed version must not be described as unchanged.

This browser helper models one exact strong-tag comparison. For example, the text '"v2"' includes quotation marks as part of the HTTP tag. Real HTTP validator parsing has additional rules outside this small exercise.
body:null in this helper means send no response body for304. It is not an instruction to send the JSON text null over HTTP.
This practice uses explicitly public content. Validators do not replace access controls or establish that personalized data is safe to share.
after: An ETag is a label for a particular version of a response. It does not have to be a date or time.
A browser can send its saved tag in the If-None-Match request header. This asks whether the saved copy is still current.
For a GET request with a matching tag, the server can send status 304: Not Modified. The browser reuses its saved copy.
If the tag is different or missing, this exercise returns status 200 with the current content and tag.
In the helper, body:null means a 304 reply has no response body. A real server must not send the JSON text null as that body.

before.question: The current tag is "v4", but a client supplies "v3". Why would a304 response be wrong here?
choices: Every tag is automatically a timestamp.
It would tell the client to reuse an older representation even though the version changed.
A304 response should carry a new full JSON body.
before.explanation: 304 means the matching stored representation can be reused; a different version requires a response carrying current content.

after.question: The current tag is "v4", but the browser sends "v3". Why is status 304 wrong here?
choices: Every tag must be a time.
It would tell the browser to reuse an older copy.
Status 304 must include a new full JSON body.
after.explanation: The tags differ, so the saved copy is old. This helper must send status 200 with the current content.

changes.before: Browser checks verify only the explicitly bounded policy helper, not complete HTTP validator parsing or a live server.
changes.after: This browser exercise checks one exact strong tag or a missing tag. Full HTTP rules also cover weak tags, lists, and wildcards. The content here is public; an ETag does not grant permission to read private content.
